---
title: "How it works"
pagetitle: "TraceGym: how it works"
---

Five stages, one guarantee: what runs in CI is byte-identical to what was
recorded, with no API keys.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  subgraph CAP[1 · Capture]
    P[OpenAI-compatible proxy] --> SP[OTel GenAI spans]
    T["@tg.tool decorator"] --> SP
    SP --> FX[Content-addressed fixtures]
  end
  CAP --> ST[(2 · Store<br/>SQLite + zstd blobs)]
  ST --> RP[3 · Replay<br/>frozen = keyless, byte-identical]
  RP --> SC
  subgraph SC[4 · Score]
    L1[L1 deterministic checks] --> AGG[Per-case score]
    L2[L2 judge ensemble<br/>cached · confidence] --> AGG
  end
  SC --> GT{5 · Gate<br/>paired bootstrap 10k}
  GT -->|block| X[Regression blocked]
  GT -->|pass| OK[Merge]
```

::: {.step}
### 1. Capture
Every side-effecting call an agent makes is recorded as an OpenTelemetry
GenAI-semconv span (`gen_ai.provider.name`, token usage, a namespaced cost) plus
a content-addressed fixture. A real `SpanExporter` also ingests spans from any
OpenTelemetry SDK.
:::

::: {.step}
### 2. Store
Rows hold SHA-256 pointers; large payloads live once in a zstd blob store, so
identical tool and LLM outputs share storage and every artifact has a stable
identity for caching and replay.
:::

::: {.step}
### 3. Replay
`frozen` mode replays fixtures with no network and no keys, byte-identically
across reruns. It refuses to run without recorded fixtures rather than fabricate.
:::

::: {.step}
### 4. Score
L1 is deterministic: schema, citation and grounding, a hardened SQL AST guard, a
SQL execution-accuracy oracle, tool-selection, trajectory, PII, and cost/latency
budgets. L2 is a cross-family judge ensemble, cached and confidence-aware, that
returns **NEEDS_REVIEW** rather than a forced verdict when the judges disagree.
:::

::: {.step}
### 5. Gate
A paired bootstrap over per-case deltas blocks a merge only on high-confidence
signals: a new invariant failure, a mean score drop whose 95% CI stays below
zero, an exact sign test on a consistent pass/fail flip, a cost regression, or
nondeterministic churn (a changed output under an identical config). Uncertain
wobbles warn, not block. The same pure predicate powers the CI gate and the
efficiency advisor.
:::

## Benchmark against a reference

The gate is an A/B benchmark engine. The reference is any run: a prior version,
an alternate model, or a deterministic **domain solver**. The SQL analyst is
graded by execution accuracy against a gold query run over the bundled database,
the standard execution-accuracy metric, at $0.

## Efficiency advisor

Beyond blocking regressions, TraceGym proposes going forward. The advisor
profiles cost, tokens, and latency, then suggests cheaper or faster
configurations. A suggestion is marked **SAFE** only after a deterministic replay
proves quality did not regress. Judge downgrades are validated by verdict
agreement, not the score gate, because letting a cheaper judge grade itself
against the gate would be circular.

## Monitor, control, optimize

The gate is the automated tier. Softer signals do not block a merge; they route
to a **human-notify** tier. A `WARN` verdict marks a mean dip whose CI still
crosses zero or a cost rise in the soft band. A review queue (`tg review`)
collects the cases the judge was unsure about and the gate warnings; resolving a
judge-review item with a label writes it to the calibration set, so a human
decision tightens the gate next time. Drift detection (`tg trend --check`) runs
EWMA and CUSUM control charts over the run history to catch a slow slide the
pairwise gate cannot see, separates an ongoing drift from a recovered excursion,
and reports the change point.

## Multi-agent trajectories

Wrap a stage in `rt.agent(name)` and the tool and LLM spans emitted inside it
nest under an agent span. Cost, latency, and tool use are then attributed per
agent by walking each span to its nearest agent ancestor, and the report draws
the trajectory as a waterfall, so a regression can be traced to the sub-agent
that caused it.
